title: PM Modi Inaugurates Vivekananda Youth Centre at Historic Mysuru Site Linked to Chicago Speech
excerpt: The new cultural centre stands where Swami Vivekananda stayed in 1892 — the visit that led to his landmark address at the World's Parliament of Religions.
body:
• PM Modi inaugurated the Swami Vivekananda Cultural Youth Centre — Viveka Smaraka — in Mysuru, Karnataka, on Saturday.
  • The centre is built at the site where Vivekananda stayed in November 1892, during the visit that led to his decision to attend the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago.
  • The facility includes a 650-seat amphitheatre, an immersive museum, yoga hall, library, and competitive examination study centre.
  • Modi urged youth to embrace a "Nation First" ethos and said India's economic growth is driven by the strength of its young population.

A Historic Site Gets a New Purpose

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated the Swami Vivekananda Cultural Youth Centre — Viveka Smaraka — in Mysuru, Karnataka, calling it a future hub for spiritual and cultural learning. The centre stands at the site where Swami Vivekananda stayed during his visit to Mysuru in November 1892, a visit regarded as pivotal because it was here that the young monk first decided to participate in the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893, according to the Times of India.

https://x.com/ANI/status/2083507219258339815

Built by the Sri Ramakrishna Ashrama with support from the central and state governments, private organisations, and devotees, the facility includes a 650-seat amphitheatre, an immersive museum on Vivekananda's life and teachings, classrooms for short-term courses, a yoga and meditation hall, a library, a competitive examination study centre, and conference rooms.

Youth Empowerment as National Strategy

Modi used the occasion to frame youth empowerment as central to India's economic trajectory. "In any country, the potential of the youth transforms into national strength only when they receive the right opportunities and direction, and the confidence to dream big and realise those dreams on their own soil," he said, according to the Times of India.

He pointed to specific metrics: India now has around 1.4 lakh MBBS seats and 823 medical colleges. The country hosts the world's third-largest startup ecosystem. The National Education Policy, he said, was preparing Indian youth for the demands of the 21st century.

"The youth of India, once in chains, today are accelerating the world's development. Today, India's economy is growing at the fastest pace because of the strength of India's youth."

— PM Narendra Modi, at the Viveka Smaraka inauguration

Vivekananda's Mysuru Connection

Modi recalled the historical significance of Mysuru in Vivekananda's journey. About 130 years ago, the then-Maharaja of Mysuru recognised the young monk's potential and extended financial support for his travels, including to the United States. "When Swami Vivekananda ji was in America, he wrote a letter from there to the then Maharaja of Mysuru. In it, he himself mentioned the Maharaja's support," Modi said.

The Prime Minister also stressed education in Indian languages, citing the NEP's provisions for studying medicine and engineering in one's mother tongue. He appealed to audiences to support local artisans, mentioning Mysuru's silk and handicrafts as suitable gifts.

Diaspora Resonance

Swami Vivekananda's 1893 Chicago address — which opened with "Sisters and brothers of America" — remains one of the most referenced moments in Indian diaspora identity. The speech introduced Hindu philosophy to a Western audience and is credited with sparking global interest in Indian spiritual traditions. The new centre's location at the exact site that precipitated that journey adds historical weight that extends well beyond Karnataka.

For NRIs and the global Indian community, the Viveka Smaraka is positioned as both a pilgrimage destination and an educational resource — a place where Vivekananda's ideals of character-building and service can be experienced in the physical context where they crystallised.

What to Watch

The centre's programming — particularly its short-term courses and competitive examination resources — will determine whether it functions primarily as a cultural monument or as an active institution shaping young lives in Karnataka and beyond.
nri_angle: Swami Vivekananda's 1893 Chicago speech is a foundational cultural touchstone for the Indian diaspora, and this centre honours the Mysuru visit that made that journey possible.
